groups.reason: A school setup administrator maintains structure, ordinary settings and calendars; lifecycle release remains a separate sign-off.
groups.allow: Maintain class/term structure, school branding and school holidays
groups.deny: Publish an academic year or edit student records with school setup authority

groups.reason: Hiring, correcting and deactivating human staff records are one workforce maintenance capability; access grants and service credentials remain separate.
groups.allow: Create, correct and archive a non-owner staff record
groups.deny: Modify grants, deactivate self or bypass owner protections

groups.reason: Editing an applied profile can change effective authority just as assigning it can; one access-administration capability avoids a misleading template-versus-assignment boundary.
groups.allow: Maintain permission profiles and assign only authority held for the complete target, scope and validity
groups.deny: Add unheld authority through a profile edit or delegate beyond the actor scope/year/validity

groups.reason: One human integration administrator owns provisioning, metadata, rotation and revocation; machine callers and read-only auditors remain excluded.
groups.allow: Provision, configure, rotate and revoke a service account within held delegation
groups.deny: Use ordinary staff maintenance or a service caller to administer credentials

groups.reason: Constructing, allocating, correcting and removing a placed curriculum is one coordinator workflow; target containment, not CRUD tokens, bounds its authority.
groups.allow: Create a grade allocation with grade authority, or maintain and synchronize completely covered class/subject allocations
groups.deny: Use one subject grant to synchronize a whole class, create a new grade-level allocation without its grade, or edit shared dictionary definitions

groups.reason: Shared subject/matter/category maintenance has one responsible administrator; dependency protection remains an invariant.
groups.allow: Create, edit and remove an unused shared subject definition
groups.deny: Change a class allocation or delete a definition with protected live dependencies

groups.reason: Correcting and archiving an existing student dossier are one registrar maintenance capability, bounded by caseload and complete affected targets.
groups.allow: Correct and archive an authorized student with all affected placements covered
groups.deny: Create an unenrolled student, edit health/notes, or archive across uncovered placements

groups.reason: An author creates and maintains their own pastoral notes; ownership and visibility restrictions continue to limit edits and deletion.
groups.allow: Create, edit and delete an own permitted note for a covered student
groups.deny: Impersonate another author, edit their note or elevate its visibility

groups.reason: A registrar maintains shared guardian identities, child links and portal-access status through one capability; child-scoped contact reads and staff access administration retain independent boundaries.
groups.allow: Create, correct and archive a shared guardian record and maintain authorized child links/portal status under existing relationship protections
groups.deny: Use child-scoped read authority or guardian self-service to alter shared access flags, or assign staff permissions through guardian management

groups.reason: Admission, transfer and withdrawal are one class-placement workflow; source and destination coverage constrain changes.
groups.allow: Enroll, transfer and withdraw when all existing/proposed class placements are covered
groups.deny: Transfer into an uncovered class or administer activity participation

groups.reason: Official incident content corrections and cancellation/cleanup belong to the class supervisor; reporting and adjudication remain separate responsibilities.
groups.allow: Correct, cancel or clean up an authorized class incident under existing state rules
groups.deny: Resolve sanctions or change an incident with an uncovered participant/placement

groups.reason: Register maintenance includes corrections, removal and recording an explanation; approving an explanation or submitted teacher correction stays separate.
groups.allow: Correct class A official attendance and record an absence explanation
groups.deny: Approve/reject an explanation, bypass submitted-correction review or alter class B

groups.reason: A subject coordinator maintains draft assessments through one capability; marks, review state and shared grading scales stay separate.
groups.allow: Create, edit and delete a covered draft assessment, subject to existing dependency/state rules
groups.deny: Edit another subject, change marks/review state or delete a protected assessment

groups.reason: Entering, editing and submitting draft marks are already alternatives in the same workflow; retain one authoring capability and a separate correction reviewer.
groups.allow: Enter, edit and submit draft marks in the authorized subject
groups.deny: Approve corrections or overwrite published/locked source marks outside the correction workflow

groups.reason: Recording and correcting draft lesson progress are one subject author workflow; review and pastoral notes remain independent.
groups.allow: Create and edit covered subject lesson/progress entries
groups.deny: Validate submitted corrections or edit student notes through logbook authority

groups.reason: Class scheduling includes creation, rescheduling and removal; whole-school calendar and activity definition administration have different target boundaries.
groups.allow: Create, reschedule and remove covered class lesson sessions
groups.deny: Change school holidays or a shared activity definition using timetable authority

groups.reason: A communications editor owns draft creation, correction and removal; sending remains a deliberate separate release capability.
groups.allow: Create, edit and remove school announcement drafts under existing state restrictions
groups.deny: Send an announcement or directly materialize delivery rows as an ordinary human

groups.reason: Viewing a class schedule includes its applicable calendar; a separate calendar-query permission provides no demonstrated independent responsibility.
groups.allow: Read class A schedule and applicable ancestor calendar
groups.deny: Read class B private events or mutate school holidays

groups.reason: Subject progress is the read projection of the same lesson logbook workflow; one scoped observation capability covers both.
groups.allow: Read/export covered subject logbook and curriculum progress
groups.deny: Read another subject or pastoral notes through lesson-progress authority

groups.reason: Opening the dashboard needs no assignable permission once every card enforces its own business read authority.
groups.allow: Open selected-profile workspace and see only cards authorized by domain reads
groups.deny: Obtain domain totals from workspace/dashboard access alone

groups.reason: An operator administrator owns account provisioning and deactivation; read-only inspection, self-protection and bounded delegation remain distinct.
groups.allow: Provision an operator with a held subset and deactivate another eligible operator
groups.deny: Deactivate self or delegate platform authority the actor does not hold

groups.reason: A platform integration administrator owns a client credential lifecycle; read-only inventory access and school-service administration stay separate.
groups.allow: Create a school-bound client, rotate its key and revoke it through admitted commands
groups.deny: Use a school owner/service account to administer platform credentials or use a revoked key

rule: Separate capabilities only for a named real workflow requiring one while denying the other, or an incompatible target boundary; retain field/state/actor constraints inside policies.

renames.reason: Assessment terminology covers homework, quizzes, projects and exams.
